R4233.summary: The cardinal de Mâcon to Montmorency: pourparlers on marriages for Pier Luigi Farnese's children, the imperial ambassador and Venice; if the French cardinals were in Rome they could steer a conclave, the pope being 'septuagenaire et plus'. He reports the mission of cardinal Verulano's secretary to Switzerland and suspects 'quelque dessaing sur le duché de Millan'.

R4234.summary: Soundings on a settlement, the bishop of Lodi's view that the King should never consent, cardinal Pisani's report, the marriages of Pier Luigi Farnese's children and the match with Cosimo de' Medici, and the arming of Pier Luigi's army (Stefano Colonna for the foot, Giovanni Battista Savelli for the horse). Pass 5 supersedes the earlier pass files, also listed.
R4234.en:

R4235.summary: 'J'ay sceu de bon lieu que le dict pape vouloit entretenir le Roy de mariage', to use the King's good words with the Emperor; Mâcon begs Montmorency to tell no one but the King and to keep the envoys' charge secret, above all from the bishop of Verona (Giberti). The three contemporary marginal decipherments agree with the reading word for word.
R4235.en:

R4238.summary: The bearer is sent by the Sienese exiles to press the King to an enterprise against Siena, which Mâcon sees no prospect in; a German at Rome claiming to be of Ferdinand's chamber offers to enter the King's service and gives him letters for a lansquenet captain with count Wilhelm von Fürstenberg.
R4238.en:
Passage 1 (f. 32v L01-L11). This bearer is sent by the exiles of Siena to the King, to persuade him to be willing to
make an enterprise against the said Siena. [clear: And although I know for certain that there is no purpose or
likelihood] in the said enterprise, I did not wish to dissuade him from his said journey, having been informed that
Duke Alessandro was busy winning them over so as to make himself master of the state of the said Siena, fearing that,
seeing themselves abandoned, they might throw themselves into the said Duke's arms.

R4239.summary: The marriage of Ottavio Farnese to the Emperor's daughter Margaret, the intrigues of the exile cardinals Salviati and Ridolfi after Alessandro de' Medici's murder, and a bid for Pier Luigi Farnese: against the Imperialists' offer of Novara, Mâcon counters with 'quelque honneste estat en France'.
R4239.en:
Letter 1 (f35r-v). [clear: I was writing to the King ... our Holy Father told me] about the marriage of the lord
Ottavio, his nephew, with the Emperor's daughter ... of the marriage of his niece with Monsieur the Count of Merle(?) ...
that he would do nothing against his neutrality, and that peace ... and the other, he would think nothing ... to corner
his neutrality; [to] take advantage of the said talks of the said lord Count. And as for Novara, the lord Pierre Luis
proceeds entirely from His Holiness, and he thinks that ... either the grant or the refusal: if he grants it, to use it
to keep up the gift to the King ... right to recover the Duchy of Milan, as, God willing, he will; if he recovers it,
to take occasion, with the coming of the Turk, to leave his neutrality. And therefore the said [?]

R4240.summary: The general council: Vergerio carried word to the Germans that they might come and speak as the Holy Spirit inspired them; the pope, judging this 'la totale ruine de l'Eglise', has sent an auditor to summon them on the old custom instead, and the Germans say pope, cardinals and bishops must first be reformed.
R4240.en:
For I have learned from a good source that Vergerio, who was nuncio of the late Pope Clement and since then appointed
by the present Pope, brought them word, before his departure from [ . ] Ferdinand, and they, on the said Pope's behalf,
as it had been written to him by His Holiness, that she was very content — as the college of the lord Cardinals is
also said to be — that, attending the said council, they might be free to say and do there as they should be inspired
by the Holy Spirit. Whereupon they had resolved to be present there, hoping to have a decisive peace there. But the
said Pope, having considered that this would be the total ruin of the Church and the Holy Apostolic See, has, moved by
counsel, dispatched an auditor of the Rota named Vuors[t] [...]

R4247.summary: Andrea Doria and Milan: Mâcon infers from Doria's letter to the conte dell'Anguillara a secret treaty between the pope and the Emperor and puts it to Paul III; then cardinal Filonardi's man sounds him on Milan passing to Pier Luigi Farnese's son or the young Sforza, and Mâcon answers that the King will never consent, Milan 'estant leur vray heritage'.
R4247.en:
and further I inform you that, having heard that Andrea Doria had sent word to the Count of Anguillara to hold his
galleys ready to join his own when he should send for him, and finding this very strange, and knowing (because the
said Count and his people had told me so, as I wrote to you before) the enmity he had with the said Doria, since
Antonio Doria, his cousin, had taken one of his fustas last summer, judging that if there was a reconciliation it was
by the Pope's command, considering even that half of the galleys that the said Count has belong to His Holiness, and
that, if this were so, it could not be without some treaty with the Emperor: I said so to His said Holiness, who
answered me that it was true that the said Count of Anguillara had let her know how the said Andrea Doria had written
him the above, at which she told me she wondered, given the capture of the said fusta;

macon1537.summary: Mâcon to Montmorency, 11 April 1537: the Farnese marriage offer (Vittoria Farnese to Cosimo de' Medici) and Paul III's threat, relayed through Latino Giovenale, to declare for the Emperor if it is refused; Pier Luigi Farnese and Novara; the King's Turkish alliance 'se verifie clerement'. The slip f. 9bis is a contemporary decipherment of the f. 9v passage, matched almost word for word. Lasry decoded this letter in 2023 but never published it.
macon1537.en:
My lord, you will see from the long letter I am writing to the King what has happened and the talks I have had with our
Holy Father since the despatch I made to him and to you on the [?6th] of this month by a courier I sent in [?part], the
said Pope […]. Further, I inform you that lord Pier Luigi [Farnese] has sent to take possession of Novara, and to the
captain of the [?citadel] of [?Pisa] to see whether he can corrupt him.

The said Pope was spoken to about the marriage [?of Cosimo] with his niece, daughter of the said Pier Luigi. It also
seems to me that if […] his will over the said marriages, the said Pope is set on throwing himself entirely into the
Emperor's devotion; but, pretending not to find them bad, His Holiness can remain more reserved, hoping to have the
support and favour of the said lord. Following [?my letter], messire Latino [Giovenale] has said so […].
